property_definitions.definition: The described use at an exact bound source unit, including its uncertainty; not its lexical grouping or an accepted meaning.
The situated context and limits of the described use, distinct from the frozen source address.
A source-described lexical grouping and its limits, not a particular spelling or accepted normalization.
A source-qualified grammatical account; unknown or competing analyses remain explicit.
A source-qualified lexical reading, not an automatically accepted philosophical concept.
The declared interpretive context and limits in which this reading is investigated.
The stated scope and boundary of the reading, preserving ambiguity and unknown alternatives.
A source-described written representation and its limits, not proof of occurrence or grammatical analysis.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
A source-grounded description of the language as a research referent, not a code or one written realization.
A described linguistic variety; dialectal or historical relationships require separate Claims.
The linguistic, social or historical criterion and its limits, not a universal test separating languages and dialects.
A source-grounded description of a writing system or explicitly scoped writing tradition, not a spoken language.
Whether the referent covers a particular sign repertoire or broader tradition; no timeless universal sign reading is implied.
A source-described notation and mapping convention, not a translation or an executed text transformation.
What the convention represents, leaves ambiguous or omits; reversibility requires evidence, not the scheme name.
The declared language of the classification term, including und when unknown; not the language of the classified work, source quotation or interface.
The declared script of the classification term; null remains unknown and does not determine a source's original script.
The attributed classification term in its declared language; it is neither a type ID nor a universal vocabulary entry.
The source-declared criteria or grounds for this classification, not an accepted proof.
The specific object, realization or passage and contextual limits to which the classification applies.
The technical media type declared for these exact file bytes by a source-item manifest; not detected format validation, literary genre, communication medium or permission to read the payload.
A source-attributed account of reception or its historical change, not an evaluation by ToS.
The particular people, community, practices and limits for which this historical account is made; not universal recognition or absence.
The documented practices of reading, response or transmission distinguishing the process; similarity alone does not establish influence.
The criteria and practices by which the historical community distinguishes an authoritative or exemplary repertoire.
Whose authority and which field this historical canon concerns; no ToS admission, correctness or universal consensus is implied.
What supports a decline or interruption in this receiving context, including surviving counterexamples and limits; database absence alone is not evidence.
For whom access or attention was renewed and what remained known or transmitted elsewhere; not the first discovery by anyone.
The source-described continuity, transformations and gaps supporting this legacy; resemblance does not establish a direct causal chain.
Source-described modern reconstruction, collation or arrangement; not the ancient referent. Required in the descriptive composite profile; native witness records retain their own source fields.
Reported editorial operations and their limits, not admission or executable code. Required in the descriptive composite profile; native witness records retain their own source fields.
Source-described extent and omissions, not an assertion of complete survival. Required in the descriptive composite profile; native witness records retain their own source fields.
The source-described textual portion and its uncertainty, not a transcription or physical artifact.
How this research distinguishes the textual portion; an editorial number does not settle original boundaries.
The particular quoted passage and attribution limits, not a general reference to a work.
Source-reported position and boundary limits; a bibliographic locator is not a resolved exact-text anchor.
Complete, fragmentary, not extant or unknown as attributed by this Claim; not certainty, admission, physical custody or access permission.
What occurred within the declared biographical scope.
Why the episode is documented as relevant to a life, with limits; significance is not causal proof.
The activities or circumstances identifying this phase, including discontinuities.
Why this research distinguishes the phase; dating and the subject's identity remain separate Claims.
The historical developments or configurations by which this periodization is described.
The research criterion, spatial scope and limitations of this periodization; rival periodizations may coexist.
The cohort as described by its source, without implying uniform experience or belief.
The specific generational criterion and its exclusions or uncertainty; individual assignment requires a separate Claim.
The scoped configuration of conditions, including what this description does not cover.
Source-described political conditions in the stated historical scope.
Source-described economic arrangements or constraints, not inferred personal wealth.
Source-described cultural practices and conditions, not uniform beliefs.
Source-described religious institutions or practices, not automatic personal adherence.
Source-described education and teaching arrangements, not automatic individual participation.
Source-described scientific practices, knowledge or technologies; availability does not prove use or influence.
The documented life condition within the stated scope.
What the source supports about the condition's relevance, distinguished from causal interpretation.
What the source cannot establish, including diagnostic and retrospective interpretation limits.
Documented bodily circumstances with attribution and uncertainty, not an unqualified diagnosis.
What this historical formation consists in, not a list of admitted participants.
The teaching or inquiry continuity distinguishing this school from an institution, a name or a general similarity class.
How the tradition is transmitted and reworked, including discontinuities; shared wording alone does not prove continuity.
The historically situated direction or undertaking distinguishing this movement from a school, tradition or mere collection of similar ideas.
The declared historical scope, distinct from the scope of an individual association Claim.
The contestable continuity criterion for this formation, not an identity decision by the reader.
The specific historical affiliation, transformation or articulation asserted, not an endorsement.
The source-declared grounds for this particular relationship, not an assessed proof.
The described relational dimension or activity, not a whole-life claim.
Source-owned historical scope wording, including unknown bounds; it supplies no normalized temporal key or capture time.
What holds this collective together; mere similarity of members is insufficient.
How membership is understood and where it is unknown or disputed; this is not a list of accepted members.
The continuing interaction or practice grounding this community, not proof of unanimous belief.
The organized roles and continuity by which this particular institutional body is described.
The stated extent and limits of this historical collective description, not a timeless definition.
The contestable criterion for retaining this collective's identity through description changes; names alone are insufficient.
What inquiry this method conducts and how; its description does not prove that it succeeds.
Declared conditions for applying the method. An empty list records no known conditions, not unconditional applicability.
What is done conceptually and what is not implied by doing it; no executable is selected.
Source-described prerequisites; an empty list means none recorded, not proof that none exist.
The conceptual movement or reframing, with its intended effect and limits.
The situation in which this movement is proposed to make sense; not universal applicability.
What is supposed for the inquiry; this is not a claim that the scenario occurred.
Conditions granted for examining the scenario, not accepted propositions; empty means none recorded.
Declared coverage of recorded assumptions; claimed completeness is not mechanically established.
What consequence or possibility is examined under the stated assumptions; it is not an unconditional conclusion.
What is presented imaginatively or figuratively and its stated scope.
The source account's characterization of the image, without imposing one aesthetic taxonomy.
The identified rhetorical arrangement and its role in the source, not a historical person or automatic interpretation.
The domain supplying the figurative presentation, not a bibliographic source locator.
What is interpreted through the figurative presentation; distinct from a software target or identity assertion.
Which aspects are proposed to carry across domains and which do not; this is an interpretation requiring assessment.
What is valued or used as a criterion of valuation, and in what sense.
Whose or which discourse's valuation is described; recording it does not adopt it.
The model or desired form and its limits; neither realization nor endorsement is implied.
How this account treats realization of the ideal, distinct from whether the description has been assessed.
What ontological commitment is described and under what substantive limits.
The source-described force, including conditional or suspended commitment; separate from assessment and admission.
What this perspective selects and leaves aside; the subject viewed through it is linked by separate grounded claims.
What is organized or distinguished by this category, within the declared philosophical scope.
The substantive tension or difficulty being investigated; its being recorded does not prove that all authors share it.
Why resolving or reframing this difficulty matters within the stated inquiry, not a compulsory project value.
What makes the grouped difficulties belong together while preserving their differences; membership is not inferred from spelling.
The interrogative content, including conditions and scope.
The presuppositions attributed to the question, or an explicit account of what is unknown. Recording them does not accept them.
The commitments or refusals that distinguish this stance, including uncertainty and limits.
In which respect the terms are differentiated; neither shared names nor graph separation supplies this criterion.
Why the terms are treated as opposed and with what limits; logical incompatibility requires its own argument.
The full proposition in this source account, including its conditions. Its presence does not assert its truth or endorsement.
Source-declared force of the proposition in this account, such as hypothetical or denied; separate from the truth and review of its description.
What reasoning is reconstructed and which limits remain; not an automatic interpretation of graph structure.
Partial, claimed_complete or unknown coverage of this argument. Claimed completeness is not mechanically proved.
The described inferential transition, not a proof that the transition preserves truth.
The source account's description of the reasoning mode; it does not select executable inference code.
What is challenged and why. Targets are separate grounded Claims; no negation of a target is inferred merely from a challenge.
The described scope and limits of this research referent; it is not a canonical definition, historical date, or causal assertion.
The explicit research criterion for retaining this semantic subject through corrected descriptions; shared names or equal record versions are not identity evidence.
Source-declared calendar, not an inferred conversion. A missing or null value is not Gregorian.
What the dating concerns. Historical time is separate from witness creation, data capture and knowledge revision.
Exact, approximate, uncertain or unknown date value. Exactness at the declared precision is not evidence that the enclosing Claim is true or accepted.
Original year-numbering declaration. Unsupported or unknown numbering is preserved without conversion to astronomical years.
Source-declared before, after, during or overlaps relative to a resolved anchor, not an inferred absolute date or causal edge.
Inclusive lower date key: astronomical year * 10000 + month * 100 + day, proleptic Gregorian only. Not a timestamp or duration; absent for unparsed or incompatible calendars.
Inclusive upper date key widened to source precision. Intersect [a,b] with start <= b AND end >= a. Missing bounds are unknown, not infinite.
Readable projected title; never an identity key.
Declared review state; not-recorded explicitly means no state was supplied, not acceptance.
Registered type closure, including this type. Contains selects a type and all its descendants.
Source-declared interval start; precision and calendar remain separate qualifiers.
Source-declared interval end; absent means unknown, not infinite.
Source-owned assertion version, distinct from entity identity and projection content revision.

types.definition: An addressable written representation in an explicitly declared notation scope, not a human display form, exact source occurrence, lemma, glyph object or meaning. Its form_identity fields preserve the represented string without silent normalization; changing that referent requires explicit identity handling.
A source-described linguistic system or variety. This organizing family does not legislate a universal language/dialect boundary; those relationships remain scoped, contestable Claims.

A persistent language research referent, distinct from its name, identifier, script, a particular utterance and the language of a description. Corrected accounts preserve identity; splitting or merging research referents requires explicit lineage.

A source-described linguistic variety distinguished by explicit linguistic, social or historical criteria. Dialect-of and historical-stage-of are separate source-grounded relationships, not automatic type ancestry or a catalog-period inference.

A writing system or explicitly bounded writing tradition, not a language, transliteration, font, glyph occurrence or timeless sign inventory. A broad cuneiform tradition may be investigated without identifying all historical sign repertoires.

A source-described convention for representing source writing in another notation. It is not translation, pronunciation, text normalization, a resulting text layer or execution of a mapping. Scheme identity does not guarantee losslessness or authorize transformation.

A source-attributed expressive or documentary form, such as article, letter, lecture, aphorism or commentary. A term may overlap with genre without making the two facets identical or assigning a new subject type.

A source-attributed carrier category of a physical artifact or bibliographic item, such as papyrus, codex or printed book. It does not identify an intellectual work, assert a chemical composition, or declare technical file encoding.
A Claim-scoped classification value with declared term, basis and scope, not a persistent subject or a type assignment.
A source-attributed genre designation of an intellectual object within a stated classification context. It does not turn a genre name into an entity subtype or atlas admission.
A source-attributed mode of communicating an intellectual object, such as spoken, written or performed expression, scoped to a realization or context; not substrate material, MIME type or genre.
Historical engagement, loss of attention, renewed access and continuing legacy in a declared receiving context; not data-ingestion history, knowledge assessment or a universal reception timeline.
A temporally developing, source-described engagement with earlier intellectual material in a declared receiving context; not mere similarity or automatic causal influence.
A historically situated process of selecting or sustaining an authoritative or exemplary repertoire; not acceptance in ToS, historical correctness or universal agreement.
A source-described decline or interruption of attention or transmission within a stated context, not absence inferred from a missing database record or proof of total loss everywhere.
A bounded episode of renewed access or attention for a specified receiving context, not first knowledge by anyone, creation of the object or restoration of its complete meaning.

A source-described persisting configuration of later uses, practices or interpretations traced to earlier intellectual material; not a possession, unchanging doctrine or automatically proved direct influence.

A modern scholarly object reconstructing, collating or arranging evidence from physical or textual witnesses. Its persistent identity is distinct from the ancient object, a physical member, source transcription, provider record and particular reading. Native member and coverage observations remain attributed metadata, not automatically admitted relations or completeness.

An independently addressable textual portion identified through a stated research boundary. It is not a piece of a physical carrier, its editorial designation, a particular quoting passage, a reconstructed reading, or an exact source-text unit. Corrected descriptions preserve the referent; competing identifications remain grounded claims.

A particular passage described as quoting another text, distinguished by its containing context and position. Identical wording quoted elsewhere does not establish the same passage. This is not the earlier fragment, a general citation, the act of quoting, the physical witness, or an exact text anchor.
A Claim-scoped report of survival for a specified intellectual object's text. This value is not a lost Work type, material copy, reconstruction or access decision.
A bounded occurrence addressed for its documented place in a person's life; not the whole biography, a diagnosis, or a causal explanation.
A source-described phase of a life identified by a stated research boundary; it need not be a single event, a homogeneous process, or a universal stage of human life.
A historically situated periodization identified through stated developments or configurations, not merely a numeric interval, a universal epoch, or an intellectual tradition.

A source-described cohort identified by a declared relation of age, historical experience or generational self-understanding; not necessarily an interacting group, an institution, a time interval, or everyone alive at once.
A scoped configuration of historically described conditions in one or more domains; not a place identity, a complete world model, or proof that context caused a thought.
A documented condition of a life, including bodily circumstances when relevant; not an agent's retrospective diagnosis, a complete medical history, or an automatic cause of philosophical content.

A source-described historical formation of intellectual inquiry, transmission or shared direction. This family does not identify a formation with its participants, doctrine, institution or atlas route.
A source-described historical teaching or inquiry formation with a specified lineage; not necessarily an institution, location or unanimous doctrine.
A historically traced continuity of reception, practice and reinterpretation across carriers and changes; not one timeless doctrine or closed collective.
A historical intellectual current organized around a specified direction of inquiry or change; not an individual thought move, institution or proof of agreement.
A historically described collective held together by specified social relations or joint activity, not a classification of people sharing an attribute.
A social group described through continuing shared practices, interaction or belonging. It need not be a legal institution, homogeneous doctrine or all people in one place.
A historically identified institution with organized roles and continuity, not a building, location, atlas category, intellectual school or abstract social institution.
A source-described way of conducting inquiry with its applicability conditions. It is not executable software, a permission grant or the atlas navigation category called Method.
A specified intellectual action in an inquiry, distinct from its occurrence in a person's life or an executable system command. Its prerequisites are source-described, not tool permissions.
An identified, potentially reusable movement within reasoning or interpretation. It need not be a deductive inference and does not become valid or historically repeated merely by being described.

An explicitly framed hypothetical scenario used to examine a question or consequence. Imagining the scenario does not establish its actuality, and accepting its assumptions for inquiry is not asserting them as facts.
An identified imagined or figurative presentation in thinking or expression, not a physical picture, a raster file or testimony that its scene occurred.
An identified arrangement or device of expression, distinct from the thought it presents, a historical figure and the effect actually produced in readers.

A rhetorical figure interpreted through a grounded cross-domain mapping. A described mapping is not literal identity, a demonstrated causal influence or an automatic property of every occurrence of the words.
An identified object or criterion of valuation within a source-described context. It is not a scalar metadata value, a metric or a value automatically endorsed by ToS.
A source-described normative or aspirational model, not evidence that an actual person or state instantiates it. An ideal may organize values without becoming a project directive.

A specified commitment about what exists or has explanatory standing within a conception, method or hypothesis. A conditional commitment does not become an unconditional doctrine or an obligation of the interchange core.
A specified perspective or dimension of a concept or conception, not a second copy of that subject or an unqualified property shared by all readings.
A source-described organizing category of thought or being within a particular inquiry. A philosophical category of time is not a technical date datatype and does not constrain the interchange core.
An identified tension or difficulty sustaining an inquiry, distinct from its interrogative formulations, a family grouping and any proposed solution.
A research grouping of distinguishable problems under an explicit criterion. Membership is grounded separately and does not make every member the same problem or require an exhaustive hierarchy.
An interrogative formulation with its presuppositions and scope, not an asserted thesis or proof that its presuppositions hold. Several questions may articulate one problem.

An identified stance in an inquiry, described by commitments, limits and relations to theses or problems. It is neither the person holding it nor a technical record status; attribution needs a separate claim.

A specified differentiation made under an explicit criterion. The two contextual term roles are separately grounded; the distinction is not automatically a partition, exclusion or claim of ontological separation.

A distinction whose terms are presented as opposed in a specified respect. Opposition does not by itself establish logical contradiction, exhaustive alternatives, temporal succession or hostility between people.

A proposition identified as content under examination, with its conditions and declared assertion force. Its formulation and truth are distinct; premise and conclusion are roles of a thesis within a specific inferential step, and a Claim about a thesis is a separate research assertion.

An identified reasoning structure described or reconstructed from evidence, possibly incompletely. Its inferential steps, targeted thesis and objections are grounded relations; neither connectedness nor an argument label proves validity, soundness or an author's endorsement.

An identified transition within an account of reasoning. Premises and conclusions are context-bound role claims pointing to theses. A step can be examined or challenged without accepting its premises, rule or result, and logical reconstruction order is distinct from historical time.

An identified challenge with substantive reasons and explicit target relations. A challenge to one premise or transition is distinct from rejection of an entire argument or conception. Its presence does not establish that the challenge succeeds or that its author is hostile.

A research referent whose explicit continuity criterion allows different situated conceptions without identifying their definitions. It is neither a bare shared name nor one definition imposed on all accounts. Membership requires grounded, contestable claims; existing scoped Concept nodes are not silently promoted to this subtype.

A situated account of thought with its own referent identity and substantive description. Attribution, conceptual membership and expression need separate grounded claims. A historical transformation relates distinct conceptions; a corrected description increments this record version without creating a new conception. A language form or a Claim about the conception is not the conception.

A persistent communicative or documentary intellectual object that need not be a Work. Its identity is distinct from a physical carrier, textual realization, catalog record and digital file. Corrected descriptions do not create another document; an attribution of shared content or identity requires a separate claim.

A document constituted as addressed correspondence. Sender, addressee, author, dispatch and reception are distinct context-bound claims, not subclasses or mandatory known facts. An unsent draft may be correspondence without an asserted dispatch; a copy is not automatically the same carrier or another letter.

A persistent physical source-object identity, including a manuscript carrier. It is not its inventory number, catalog record, intellectual work, reconstructed composite, transcription or digital representation. Description changes do not change the artifact ID. Source metadata navigation alone does not assert any carrier-to-text, custody or historical relation.
Root for source-described happenings, developments and persisting conditions in the historical world; not semantic Event/State, a dating assertion, or a provenance activity.

A source-described occurrence treated as one happening. Its identity is independent of labels, disputed dating, participants, and correction of its description. An interpretation of its significance is a separate claim.
A source-described temporally developing process. Its phases, participants, and relation to events require claims; a long event is not retyped by duration alone.
A source-described persisting condition in a historical scope. It is not an authored semantic State, an absence inferred from missing events, or a causal explanation.
Exact version-bound text-layer representation; not the underlying Work.
Version-bound source selector. Offsets belong to this exact layer, not a mutable document.
A source-layout or method-proposed unit. Unit kind and boundary posture remain qualifiers, never lexical identity.

A particular source-bound use with a correctable research description and immutable native TextUnit binding. Its identity is distinct from its lexical form, Lexeme, sense, underlying evidence unit and description revision. Native unit granularity and proposed boundaries do not become accepted linguistic analysis.

A persistent lexical research referent independent of spelling, occurrence, a particular sense and philosophical concept. Lexical grouping is an analysis, not string equality; corrected accounts preserve the subject while incompatible referents need explicit lineage.

A situated lexical reading retained as its own research referent, not a lexeme, philosophical concept, canonical definition or one usage token. Sense-of and interpretation-of links are separately grounded Claims; descriptions may be corrected without merging competing readings.
Source-declared sign identity with its admission status and competing interpretations.
Versioned stand-off annotation or segmentation packet; not source-text authority.
Claim under the semantic annotation v2 contract, preserving proposition, evidence, maker, alternatives and review refs.
Evidence for an annotation claim with direction, role and exact source anchors.
Source-owned review event scoped to claims or segmentations; never inferred from a status label.
An addressable source relation assertion linked to its exact supporting claim.
Root of the semantic interchange hierarchy; it does not assert one philosophical ontology.
An object whose ToS identity persists while versioned descriptions and assertions may change.
A persistent person-like responsibility bearer; author, translator and editor remain relation roles rather than subclasses.
A persistent collective or institutional identity participating in source claims.
Root for persistent intellectual creations, communicative documents, realizations and aggregates. The bibliographic ladder is one profile under this root, not a required shape for every document.
An abstract intellectual or artistic creation, distinct from language realization, edition, acquired item and file.
A language- or version-specific realization of one Work.
Root for edition and collection identities that embody or aggregate Expressions and Works.
A published or edited manifestation, distinct from one acquired copy.
An aggregate publication or container with evidence-bearing membership claims.
One physical or digital acquired copy or container.
One immutable byte sequence addressed by its declared digest.
A versioned observed access or authority link; it is not the object it points to.
Root for authored ToS node classes; it does not make branch candidates canonical.
An authored source-grounded semantic node, distinct from a bibliographic Work or source file.
A source-returnable concept node or an explicitly pre-canon concept candidate.
An authored principle node.
An authored lineage or movement path between semantic objects.
An authored semantic event; event identity is distinct from its temporal assertions.
An authored semantic state.
An authored support or contextual grounding node.
An authored contextual node.
An authored analogy node.
An authored reviewed synthesis node.
A versioned assertion whose identity, evidence and review posture remain separate from its subject and object.
A reified evidence-bearing assertion with its own version, maker, provenance and review state.
Root for explicit temporal assertions, instants and intervals; raw period labels remain unparsed candidates.
A claim-scoped temporal value with an explicit calendar, facet, precision and uncertainty posture where available.
A normalized point-like temporal value within a declared calendar and precision.
A normalized start/end temporal value with separate boundary precision and meaning.
A claim-scoped publication, manufacture or distribution activity preserving literal statement, roles, places and time.
A value scoped to a claim and not promoted into persistent identity.
A literal place statement kept distinct from a normalized Place identity.
Root for evidence, review, provenance and maker representations supporting claims.
A source-returnable evidence reference supporting or challenging a claim.
A distinct review event or decision over an assertion.
A versioned activity recording how a source or claim representation was produced.
The recorded human, model or system responsibility representation that made a claim.
Root for normalized place identity and claim-scoped spatial references; navigation Regions remain separate.
A persistent normalized Place identity; its names, boundaries and historical validity remain versioned assertions.
A tree or atlas navigation object that must not be mistaken for a persistent domain identity.
A branch-shaped navigation object in the source tree.
An atlas era route; it is not by itself a normalized temporal interval.
A branch region used for navigation; it is not automatically a geographic Place or containment fact.
A source-tree tradition route.
A pre-canon philosophy projection category for a school or tradition.
A source-owned link between a philosophy branch and a source-witness backlog anchor.
A source-facing witness identity not yet resolved to a more specific public semantic type.
Root for pre-canon philosophy atlas categories; these types stabilize interchange without canonizing instances.
A pre-canon figure anchor, not yet necessarily a normalized Agent identity.
A pre-canon institution category, distinct from a normalized Organization record.
A pre-canon text-corpus category, not a Work, Collection or acquired Item by implication.
A pre-canon controversy or contested-reading category.
A pre-canon genre classification candidate.
A pre-canon medium category.
A pre-canon combined language or script category; normalization may later split the two.
A pre-canon transmission channel category.
A pre-canon method category.
A pre-canon preservation-state category.
A pre-canon combined civilization or literary-complex category.
A pre-canon object whose chronology, geography or evidence posture cannot yet be represented as an ordinary branch.
A pre-canon artifact navigation anchor, not a normalized physical artifact identity by implication.
Atlas, graph-view, table and dossier projection metadata rather than a domain entity.
A repository topology or resource representation, never the domain object described by its file.
The root of the repository topology projection.
A branch representation from the ToS source-home manifest.
A manifest-file representation in the repository topology.
A file or generated-resource representation in the repository projection.
A projection placeholder whose source-local endpoint exists but whose full entity representation is not available in this carrier.
Explicit fallback for a source-native kind that has no reviewed semantic interchange mapping yet.
